paths.description: Homepage hot-feed template, global navigation, sign-in, preferences, narrow viewport, performance, network, security, accessibility, and repeated scroll.
Representative public story/detail template and content reading journey.
Primary authoring entry point; confirms the anonymous authentication gate and its recovery/sign-in state.

findings.summary: The sticky site chrome does not adapt as the user scrolls.
findings.evidence: DOM evidence reports a sticky header, but platform-probe.json and CSS inspection found no scroll-state or scroll-timeline rules; the header remains a fixed 64px chrome region.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a scroll-state container query or a restrained shrinking-header treatment, while preserving reduced-motion behavior.

findings.summary: Advertising displaces the primary feed before users reach content.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots show a roughly 200px top ad/empty ad slot before navigation and content; themes-desktop.png shows a full-width banner dominating the first viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve a smaller, stable ad slot below primary navigation, label ads clearly, and avoid loading an empty interruption above content.

findings.summary: Non-content chrome and advertising consume too much of the first viewport.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots devote the top 200px to advertising and a 300px right rail to sign-in/promotional chrome, leaving a narrow 541px content column.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce persistent side chrome and top advertising so the feed or article is the dominant first-viewport surface.

findings.summary: The desktop layout is forced into mobile viewports.
findings.evidence: At a 360px viewport, layout evidence reports scrollWidth 900, clientWidth 360, and 540px horizontal overflow. Mobile screenshots show most navigation and content clipped off-screen.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the 900px minimum layout with intrinsic fluid sizing, mobile navigation, and reflowing columns; verify no overflow at 320-400px.

findings.summary: Components do not adapt to their available container.
findings.evidence: platform-probe.json found zero container rules, while the 360px layout remains 900px wide and cards/right rail retain desktop dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Add container types and size-aware component rules so feed cards, navigation, auth panels, and sidebars recompose rather than clip.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and touch target support are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The accessibility probe found 40 sampled controls below 24px in one dimension; focused login buttons and inputs computed to outline: none. Lighthouse target-size scored 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide visible :focus-visible styles and at least 24x24 CSS px targets, preferably 44x44 for primary touch controls; retain non-hover affordances.

findings.summary: Empty login submission gives no visible recovery feedback.
findings.evidence: After activating “Войти” with empty fields, login-invalid.png is visually unchanged: fields have no visible required message, invalid state, or recovery instruction.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after submission/interaction, mark fields with aria-invalid, associate concise messages, and announce a summary in a live region.

findings.summary: Load and interaction readiness are far outside good ranges.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 17.5s, TBT 2,590ms, Speed Index 8.5s, and time-to-interactive 19.8s; the trace also measured 980.52ms blocking time.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile LCP discovery and INP/TBT causes, then prioritize the LCP resource and split/defer non-critical work.

findings.summary: Long JavaScript tasks block the main thread.
findings.evidence: Trace evidence found 7 long tasks, a 482.9ms maximum, and 980.52ms total blocking time; mobile layout observation found tasks up to 506ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Break long tasks into scheduler-yielding chunks, defer ad/analytics initialization, and remove unnecessary startup execution.

findings.summary: The critical path ships a large parser-discovered script chain.
findings.evidence: HAR evidence records 145 requests and 3.53MB transferred; parser-discovered app/vendor scripts are high priority, and the main document took 1.41s.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit actual script attributes, defer non-critical bundles, preload only proven critical assets, compress the DDoS script response, and shorten dependency chains.

findings.summary: Large amounts of unused code are delivered on initial load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 1,041KiB unused JavaScript and 98KiB unused CSS; HAR shows 2.36MB of transferred script across 31 requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Use coverage to split route/editor/advertising code, load optional dependencies conditionally, and remove duplicate or legacy bundles.

findings.summary: Controls, fields, links, and images lack accessible names or alternatives.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse button-name and link-name audits scored 0; the probe found 10 unlabeled visible inputs, and images evidence reports 12 missing alt attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use explicit labels and accessible names, remove empty interactive links, and add meaningful alt text or empty alt for decoration.

findings.summary: Some text and essential UI fail minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse color-contrast scored 0. The forced-colors screenshot remains operable, but normal-theme combinations still fail automated contrast analysis.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust normal-theme foreground/background tokens to WCAG AA while preserving the working forced-colors treatment.

findings.summary: Focus indication is removed from important interactive controls.
findings.evidence: The focus probe computed outline:none for login buttons and both username/password fields, while the homepage has no h1 and Lighthouse accessibility scored 0.58.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore strong :focus-visible outlines, keep focus order aligned with reading order, and add one descriptive h1 to the feed template.

findings.summary: The page does not reflow at a narrow/zoom-equivalent viewport.
findings.evidence: The 360px capture exposes a 900px layout and 540px overflow; Lighthouse target-size scored 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement responsive reflow without horizontal scrolling and enlarge small targets; verify at 320 CSS px and 200% zoom.

findings.summary: Image sizing and asset structure leave avoidable layout/resource risk.
findings.evidence: The images primitive reports 27 of 27 images without both width and height attributes, 17 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, and 6 oversized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width/height or aspect-ratio, lazy-load below-fold images, and serve appropriately sized responsive sources.

findings.summary: The page has deprecations, inspector issues, and BFCache blockers.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports one deprecation warning, inspector issues, and two BFCache failure reasons.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve the specific Lighthouse deprecation/Inspector entries and remove unload/cache-control or runtime blockers that prevent BFCache.

findings.summary: Some links are not crawlable and the public templates are not mobile-friendly.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse crawlable-anchors scored 0; the DOM includes empty links, while the 360px viewport clips navigation and content despite a valid viewport meta tag.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href anchors with descriptive text and make all public templates reflow on mobile.

findings.summary: Rich content lacks structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe found Open Graph tags but no JSON-LD. A public story/article archetype should expose Article and author/date metadata matching visible content.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org JSON-LD for WebSite/Organization and Article entities, retaining Open Graph metadata.

findings.summary: Cookies are not consistently protected despite HTTPS.
findings.evidence: cookies.json reports 33 cookies without Secure, including PHPSESS, and widespread SameSite=None; headers show HTTPS/HSTS but no X-Content-Type-Options.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure on every HTTPS cookie, use explicit Lax/Strict defaults unless cross-site use is required, retain HttpOnly for session cookies, and add nosniff.

findings.summary: The page loads a large, chatty third-party tracking surface by default.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 36 third-party origins and Google/DoubleClick trackers; HAR counted 139 third-party requests and 3.29MB transferred, including multiple analytics/ad cookie-sync chains.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize vendors, gate non-essential tracking on consent, batch analytics, and defer advertising/analytics until needed.

findings.summary: Public authentication relies on passwords or federated providers without a passkey path.
findings.evidence: The visible sign-in surface offers password, Yandex ID, and VK ID; platform/DOM evidence found no WebAuthn or passkey affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey registration and authentication as a phishing-resistant option, with password/federation as recovery fallbacks.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive headers are incomplete.
findings.evidence: headers.json shows missing X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy. CSP contains upgrade-insecure-requests and frame-ancestors but no script/style/default source restrictions.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP, nosniff, strict Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; preserve clickjacking and HSTS controls.

findings.summary: The app-like social experience has a service worker but no install manifest.
findings.evidence: platform-probe.json found a registered service worker but no manifest link, and /manifest.json returned 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a valid web app manifest and verify an intentional offline fallback for feed/story navigation, or explicitly scope the service worker to non-PWA duties.

findings.summary: Advertising is visually dominant and not consistently identified as advertising.
findings.evidence: First-viewport screenshots show large promotional banners and an inline job promotion presented as page content without an obvious “Advertisement” label.
findings.suggestedFix: Label paid placements unambiguously, visually separate them from posts, and keep primary content ahead of promotional calls to action.

findings.summary: Login validation does not explain empty required fields.
findings.evidence: The empty-submit screenshot shows no visible field-level error, while the accessibility probe finds placeholder-only unlabeled inputs.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native required constraints or interaction-timed custom validation, visible messages, aria-describedby, aria-invalid, and accessible error announcements.

findings.summary: Sign-in autocomplete metadata is incomplete.
findings.evidence: The username uses autocomplete=username, but the password field has no current-password token; several account recovery fields have empty or generic autocomplete values.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply current-password, new-password, email, one-time-code, and other precise autocomplete tokens to each account field.

findings.summary: Images are not consistently resolution- or delivery-optimized.
findings.evidence: Images evidence found 6 oversized images, 10 without srcset, 4 legacy-format images, and 17 below-fold images not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide responsive srcset/sizes, modern formats, intrinsic dimensions, and lazy loading for below-fold content.

findings.summary: Startup performs substantial non-essential ad and analytics work.
findings.evidence: HAR shows 52 fetch/XHR requests and many ad/analytics sync redirects; the trace records 980.52ms blocking time and Lighthouse finds more than 1MB unused JS.
findings.suggestedFix: Deprioritize and conditionally load background analytics/ads, batch telemetry, and stop cookie-sync chains that do not serve the immediate task.

findings.summary: Third-party code dominates the page budget.
findings.evidence: 139 of 145 HAR requests are classified off the main origin and account for 3.29MB of 3.53MB transferred; tracker evidence lists 36 third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party request/byte budget, remove low-value vendors, self-host suitable assets, and defer media/ads until they enter the viewport.

findings.summary: The initial memory footprint is high for a text-first feed.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary reports 1,068,025 nodes and 62.8MB self size. The post-scroll snapshot did not grow, but the one-state footprint remains large.
findings.suggestedFix: Use heap allocation/retainer analysis to reduce feed DOM, virtualize off-screen posts, and remove heavyweight ad/widget objects.

Cut startup JavaScript, long tasks, and critical-path work
Secure cookies and deploy complete browser policies
Repair accessible names, labels, focus, and contrast
Add humane login validation and precise autocomplete
Reduce advertising dominance and label promotions
Add structured data and a valid app manifest
Make sticky navigation react to scroll state
